data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -o somd-array-gpu-%A.%a.out
#   -p main
#   -n 1
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --time 24:00:00

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=24h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p main (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or on different hardware (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: -o somd-array-gpu-%A.%a.out
# Slurm tokens %A (array master job id) and %a (array index) are not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

echo "CUDA DEVICES:" $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES

mkdir -p 10cycles
cd 10cycles

export OPENMM_PLUGIN_DIR=/home/julien/sire.app/lib/plugins/

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, run within the allocation (optionally via flux run -n 1).
~/sire.app/bin/somd-freenrg -C ../sim10.cfg -l 0.50 -p CUDA

reasons: The original Slurm job required a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job specified a partition (`-p main`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -o somd-array-gpu-%A.%a.out
#SBATCH -p main
#SBATCH -n 1
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --time 24:00:00

echo "CUDA DEVICES:" $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES

mkdir 10cycles
cd 10cycles

export OPENMM_PLUGIN_DIR=/home/julien/sire.app/lib/plugins/

srun ~/sire.app/bin/somd-freenrg -C ../sim10.cfg -l 0.50 -p CUDA
cd ..
